Tags.rationale: ExoskeletonsNormal.cs:18 declares EncounterTag.Exoskeletons. `_hive_rooms()` pins the identical tag under "exoskeletons_normal". Tag-based no-repeat picking lives at the room/act picker layer (seam/rooms_and_map), not on the sim's `Encounter` object; verified only that the declared tag transcribes correctly.

Slots.maps_to: exoskeleton.py::ExoskeletonsEncounter._SLOTS = ("first","second","third","fourth") used as a per-monster constructor arg
Slots.rationale: ExoskeletonsNormal.cs:20 => ["first","second","third","fourth"], and unlike Bowlbugs/Decimillipede/KaiserCrab in this same batch, the slot string here IS load-bearing: `Exoskeleton.cs:61-65`'s `ConditionalBranchState("INIT_MOVE")` gates the opening move directly on `base.Creature.SlotName` ("first"->SKITTER, "second"->MANDIBLES, "third"->ENRAGE, "fourth"->random RAND branch). The sim reproduces the outcome by a different mechanism: `Exoskeleton.__init__` takes a `slot: str` constructor argument (exoskeleton.py:39-49) and its own `build_machine`'s `ConditionalBranchState("INIT_MOVE")` (exoskeleton.py:61-68) branches on `self.slot` with the identical four string values and identical per-slot move mapping. `ExoskeletonsEncounter.create_monsters` (exoskeleton.py:97-100) constructs `Exoskeleton(hooks, rng, slot=self._SLOTS[i]) for i in range(self.count)` with `count=4` for the Normal variant and `_SLOTS=("first","second","third","fourth")` -- same 4 strings, same positional assignment order as the C# array literal. The sim never sets `Creature.slot_name` itself (bypassing `Encounter.Slots`/`SortEnemiesBySlotName` entirely), but since the only C# reader of `Exoskeleton`'s own SlotName is its own move-selection logic (confirmed: no other monster/power file in this fight reads it), and the constructor-arg route reproduces that exact per-position outcome, the observable behavior matches.

RoomType.rationale: ExoskeletonsNormal.cs:22 => RoomType.Monster. "exoskeletons_normal" sits in `_hive_rooms().normal_keys` and nowhere else, matching this batch's pool-classification convention.

HasScene.maps_to: no counterpart -- sim is headless, no Godot scene graph
HasScene.rationale: ExoskeletonsNormal.cs:24 => true. Purely a rendering-asset gate (`ScenePath`/`CreateScene()`), no headless equivalent, no gameplay consequence, same as every other HasScene=true unit in this batch.

AllPossibleMonsters.maps_to: no per-encounter counterpart; full_env.py::_monster_classes() (global Monster-subclass walk)
AllPossibleMonsters.rationale: ExoskeletonsNormal.cs:26 declares a single-element list containing only `Exoskeleton` -- exactly GenerateMonsters' draw space (four copies of the one class). Same consumer census as the rest of the batch: the property's only two real readers are UI/debug (dev-console unlock list, bestiary ratio); the sim's real vocabulary need is met by the global `_monster_classes()` walk. Cost: none observed.

GenerateMonsters.rationale: ExoskeletonsNormal.cs:28-37: four fixed `Exoskeleton` instances in slots "first","second","third","fourth" in that literal order, zero RNG draws. `ExoskeletonsEncounter.create_monsters` (exoskeleton.py:97-100) returns `[Exoskeleton(hooks, rng, slot=self._SLOTS[i]) for i in range(self.count)]` with `count=4`, producing the same 4 instances in the same slot order, zero draws (no `selection_rng` branch in this override). Roster (4x Exoskeleton), order, per-slot assignment and draw count all match.

ShouldReceiveCombatHooks.rationale: `EncounterModel.cs:39` default (`=> false`), not overridden by the sealed `ExoskeletonsNormal`. The sim's `Encounter` is never a hook listener.

guards.what: Gold ladder (MinGoldReward/MaxGoldReward) and ShouldGiveRewards -- both inherited, not overridden by ExoskeletonsNormal
guards.rationale: RoomType.Monster => 10-20 gold, matched by `rewards.py:170-173`'s `GOLD_REWARD_RANGES[RoomType.MONSTER]` (non-ascension baseline; Poverty scaling out of scope). `ShouldGiveRewards` default `true` matched by `Encounter.should_give_rewards`'s dataclass default, unmodified by `EXOSKELETONS_NORMAL = ExoskeletonsEncounter(id="exoskeletons_normal", count=4)`.
